title: HARLens
summary: Offline HAR triage for failed, slow, and domain-heavy requests.
problem: Developers receiving a browser HAR capture need a quick first-pass summary of failed and slow requests without uploading the file or reopening a full browser debugging session.
audience: Web developers and support engineers inspecting exported HTTP Archive files locally.
why_now: Chrome DevTools supports exporting network activity as HAR; these captures remain useful portable inputs for local network triage and may contain private request data.
difference: HARLens produces a terminal or JSON summary from an existing HAR using only Python's standard library, with no service, browser session, or upload required.
monetization_hypothesis: Best kept as a free local utility; a paid reporting workflow would need separate demand validation.
limitations: It summarizes recorded metadata only and does not replay requests, render a waterfall, or diagnose security issues.
Aggregate request time adds individual durations and is not page-load time; transfer totals use bodySize with a content.size fallback and exclude headers.
The CLI assumes HAR-shaped JSON and can show a Python traceback for malformed inputs; it does not redact URLs.

alternatives.name: Chrome DevTools Network panel
alternatives.difference: DevTools provides interactive request details and waterfall analysis; HARLens offers a concise terminal/JSON summary of an existing file without a browser session.

alternatives.name: HAR Viewer
alternatives.difference: HAR Viewer visualizes HTTP Archive logs in a web application; HARLens focuses on read-only local command-line triage with no frontend or server.
